items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: As Russel was not working regularly, I accepted and told Russel who agreed that I should do it and wished me luck.

ctx.x: As I said already, I had known Gus McClung for many years but I never saw him as happy as he was after I had done '......anything but love' for those two shows. The rest of the band, the chorus girls and stage hands were all smiles for me. Ralph asked me if I would do the show the next day and I accepted. I went straight home after the dance because the first show was at 11 o'clock the next morning and I wanted to get as much rest as possible.

The four shows on Thursday went down great and Ralph had some theater dates to do the following week in New Jersey and I did them with him. After those dates he was going on a theater tour and asked me if I would stay with the band. As Russel was not working regularly, I accepted and told Russel who agreed that I should do it and wished me luck.

Ralph had signed a contract with R.K.O. which was the biggest theatrical circuit in the country. There were three tap dancers; Blain, Rice and Berry known as the Three Sams; Bessie Dudley, who was a snake hip dancer and the band. Ralph danced and also did a parody on 'Penthouse Serenade'. Ralph was a very handsome light-coloured man and sort of stocky for a tap dancer. He had teamed with a dancer named Eddie Rector who was one of the best that ever wore a pair of dancing shoes.
